title: Writing Expressions from Words
short: "3 times the sum of 8 and 7" is 3 × (8 + 7).
trouble: Children write 3 × 8 + 7, leaving out the parentheses that the words call for.

blocks.html: Now that you can work with parentheses, brackets and braces, you can turn words into expressions. Words like sum, difference, product and quotient each name one result: the answer to an addition, a subtraction, a multiplication or a division.

Write the operations in the order the words ask for. If a step the words do first would not come first by the order of operations, put it in parentheses: “3 times the sum of 8 and 7” is $3 \times (8 + 7)$.
“The sum of 8 and 7” is one amount, 15. Three times that amount is three groups of 15. Without parentheses, $3 \times 8 + 7$ would multiply first and add 7 only once, which is a different amount.

blocks.name: tapediagram
blocks.cap: Three times the sum of 8 and 7: three equal pieces, each $8 + 7$.

blocks.title: Words to an expression
blocks.q: Write “add 6 and 9, then multiply by 4” and find its value.
steps: The words add first. Multiplying would normally come first, so the sum needs parentheses: $(6 + 9) \times 4$.

blocks.title: No parentheses needed
blocks.q: Write “5 less than the product of 7 and 3.”
steps: “5 less than” it means take 5 away from it: $7 \times 3 - 5$.
Multiplying comes first anyway, so no parentheses are needed. The value is $21 - 5 = 16$.

blocks.title: Compare without calculating
steps: $4 \times$ that amount is 4 groups of it.
blocks.a: It is 4 times as large, and you never had to add.

blocks.html: Writing $3 \times 8 + 7$ for “3 times the sum of 8 and 7.” Check by reading your expression back in words: $3 \times 8 + 7$ says “multiply 3 by 8, then add 7,” which is not what you were told.
